summary: The bad flow takes an attacker-controlled environment variable (ADD) and concatenates it directly onto an uploads root directory to build a File path, allowing relative path traversal (e.g. ../../etc/passwd) out of the intended directory. I added a canonical-path containment check in the sink so that only files resolving inside the uploads root are read; legitimate filenames under the uploads directory continue to work, while traversal sequences are rejected before the file is opened.
